newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen tad easier, yen swap firmer in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen tad easier, yen swap firmer in Tokyo.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen contract on TIFFE was easier at the close of the day session in Wednesday in line with bearish JGBs, traders said.
Yen interest rate swap (IRS) rates firmed, particularly in the two-year zone, as some trust banks received fixed interest rates.
The two-year IRS was quoted at 0.88-0.92 percent, up from 0.86-0.90 percent in late Tuesday trading.

"The perception gap as to the outlook for the economy between the government and the market appears to be narrowing, causing losses in JGBs and Euroyen prices," said a chief trader at a local brokerage firm.

Traders said that although Bank of Japan (BOJ) officials had been saying recently that the basis for the recovery was getting firmer, at least in the near-term, the market had been ignoring the remarks.
"But, in the past few weeks, there have been more traders willing to listen to the BOJ's opinion, which is bearish for the overall debt market," the trader said.
Market talk that the Japanese government could face new scandal revelations added to nervousness in the Euroyen market, which was already jittery over losses in Tokyo stocks and JGBs.
In the cash market, the key three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.50-0.51 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.49 percent, also unchanged from Tuesday.

In the Euro interbank markets, the Japan premium -- the extra cost of funding for Japanese banks -- has been resurfacing after the banks' interim results announced last month showed they were still exposed to a large amount of bad loans.
Even major Japanese city banks with relatively good ratings have been paying some 20 basis points above the prevailing one-month Eurodollar deposit rate of 5.50 percent.
Smaller banks are estimated to be paying much larger premiums, traders said.
